title: Service contract corridor + probe-gating for adaptive error-budget allocation
creator: Nora Chen
description: PRD to define a ‘service contract corridor’ concept: a multi-band SLA envelope (green/yellow/red) that maps latency and availability targets to adaptive error-budget allocations per tenant class. This ticket scopes acceptance criteria, rollout probes, canary exit conditions, and the automated gating logic that will be enforced by the Console and runtime orchestration. The goal is to allow progressive rollouts of model or runtime changes while automatically throttling or rolling back when tenant-weighted error budgets breach defined corridors.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Define explicit numeric targets for p50/p95/p99 latency and availability for three corridor bands (green/yellow/red) for interactive text-generation and embeddings endpoints.
A2: Specify tenant classification rules (free / standard / enterprise) and how error budgets are apportioned and weighted across tenants.
A3: Produce a probe plan (synthetic + production-sampled) with measurement windows and statistical thresholds for canary promotion/exit.
A4: Implement rollout gating policy language (canary size, observation window, burn-rate thresholds, automated fallback) and document expected runtime behavior and operator overrides.
A5: End-to-end test plan that demonstrates automated rollback when tiered error-budget burn exceeds thresholds with synthetic load and a controlled traffic shift.
A6: Console UI copy and acceptance tests for the new corridor view and gating controls; visualizes per-tenant burn and aggregate corridor state.
A7: Security review completed for telemetry and tenant weighting logic; KMS/PII considerations documented.
A8: Runbook added to oncall playbook with exact alert thresholds and mitigation steps for corridor breaches.
A9: Release notes and customer-facing SLA table prepared for Hosted API customers and sales collateral for Dedicated/Private prospects.
A10: Stakeholder signoff from Runtime, Console, Observability, and Legal teams.
decisions: D1: Use weighted error-budget allocation where enterprise tenants consume proportional share but have higher burn tolerance for critical traffic.
D2: Canary promotion requires two consecutive observation windows (5m and 30m) within the selected corridor thresholds before expanding traffic.
D3: Rollback triggers are deterministic: breach of red-corridor availability OR sustained p99 > red threshold for observation window OR burn-rate > 3x baseline for > 10m.
D4: Console will show corridor state and enable manual override with a required comment and audit log entry.
D5: For Dedicated customers we expose corridor parameters as configurable knobs; Hosted has conservative defaults.
D6: Adopt synthetic probes that run from multiple regions to capture network/regional variance as a gating signal (not sole signal).
tradeoffs: T1: Aggressive canary gating reduces incidents but slows time-to-ship for low-risk changes (longer observation windows required).
T2: Tenant-weighted budgets improve fairness but add complexity to billing/observability and may require data-model changes in Console.
T3: Exposing corridor knobs for Dedicated increases customer flexibilty but raises support burden and policy complexity.
T4: Relying on synthetic probes improves signal coverage but can have false positives; balanced by combining with sampled production traffic.
rollout_gates: Probe stage: infra and synthetic probes (size 1–5 rps across regions) for 15m. Must meet green or yellow corridor thresholds to proceed.
Micro-canary: 1% production traffic for 30m (observation windows: 5m & 30m). Metrics evaluated: p95/p99 latency, availability, token error rate, CPU/GPU throttling signals.
Canary ramp 1: 5% for 30m. Automated evaluation: burn-rate check (<=1.5x baseline) AND corridor not in red.
Canary ramp 2: 25% for 60m. Automated evaluation: must sustain green/yellow corridor and no sustained p99 elevation.
Full rollout: 100% after two successful ramps and operator approval if any yellow windows were present.
Immediate abort: Any red-corridor breach triggers automated rollback to last-good variant and opens an incident if burn-rate threshold crossed.
Manual override: Product/Eng can force promotion with mandatory comment; manual overrides create a temporary elevated alerting threshold and require post-mortem.
monitoring_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) per endpoint and per tenant class
token error rate and model runtime exceptions
request queue depth and batch latency
synthetic probe success rate and regional variance
